cohort: The study included 141 pregnant women diagnosed with hypertensive disorders, selected from a screening of 1059 women at a tertiary care center.
finding: Preeclampsia and eclampsia significantly increase maternal and neonatal complications compared to gestational and chronic hypertension, outlining a clear risk continuum.
mod_finding: The preeclampsia/eclampsia group demonstrated significantly higher rates of Caesarean deliveries (64.6%).
birth_weight: 2950.6 g (average for low birth weight in the preeclampsia/eclampsia group)
